rv.q: “Kim’s Convenience,” now playing at The Old Globe through June 14, delivers a warm and funny portrait of family, community, and the complicated push and pull between tradition and change.
Not only is Kim’s Convenience super fun to watch with a very high laugh per minute rate, the play actually came first!
It's a touching slice-of-life story that anyone, particularly those from immigrant families, will relate to.
Mengesha’s comical rendition of Kim’s Convenience, features plenty of laughter and warmth, providing an emotionally rich experience in Balboa Park.
Kim’s Convenience has all the elements of a really fine show: good script, great direction and beautiful comic timing.
It is a funny, heartwarming family drama that offers a familiar portrait of a Korean family in the early 2000s.

cn.t: Critics find this warm, funny family comedy charming and heartfelt, with acute observations about immigration and generational conflict. The plot may be thin, but strong characters and everyday humor make it an enjoyable slice-of-life portrait.
